namespace Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection

    /// <summary>
    /// Registers every validator this assembly generated.
    /// </summary>
    public static class GeneratorTestsValidationExtensions
    {

        /// <summary>
        /// Adds this assembly's generated validators, and a validation runner for each
        /// validated type.
        ///
        /// Not idempotent. Calling this twice registers every validator twice, and a
        /// runner merges every registered validator for a type - so each error would be
        /// reported twice. Add rather than TryAdd is deliberate: registering a second
        /// validator for one type is how a hand-written rule composes with the generated
        /// one, so this cannot dedupe without breaking that.
        /// </summary>
        public static global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection AddGeneratorTestsValidators(this global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.IServiceCollection services)
        {
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceCollectionServiceExtensions.AddSingleton<global::ValidationModules.IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Address>, global::Sample.AddressValidator>(services);
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceCollectionServiceExtensions.AddSingleton<global::ValidationModules.IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Line>, global::Sample.LineValidator>(services);
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceCollectionServiceExtensions.AddSingleton<global::ValidationModules.IValidatorFor<global::Sample.Order>, global::Sample.OrderValidator>(services);

            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ValidationModulesServiceCollectionExtensions.AddValidationRunner<global::Sample.Address>(services);
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ValidationModulesServiceCollectionExtensions.AddValidationRunner<global::Sample.Line>(services);
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ValidationModulesServiceCollectionExtensions.AddValidationRunner<global::Sample.Order>(services);

            // Element-wise validation for collection bodies - List<T> and T[] - so a batch
            // endpoint's .Validate<List<T>>() resolves a validator that walks the elements
            // with indexed paths. Closed per type, for the AOT reason above.
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ValidationModulesServiceCollectionExtensions.AddCollectionValidatorsFor<global::Sample.Address>(services);
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ValidationModulesServiceCollectionExtensions.AddCollectionValidatorsFor<global::Sample.Line>(services);
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ValidationModulesServiceCollectionExtensions.AddCollectionValidatorsFor<global::Sample.Order>(services);

            // TryAdd, so a namer the consumer registered first survives. The policy here is
            // the one the literals above were emitted with, so the engines that resolve a
            // namer at run time agree with the generated code by default.
            global::Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Extensions.ServiceCollectionDescriptorExtensions.TryAddSingleton<global::ValidationModules.Naming.IValidationFieldNamer>(services, global::ValidationModules.Naming.CamelCaseFieldNamer.Instance);

            return services;
        }
